49: ## Specification fields
50: 
51: Use [the authoring template](../templates/authoring.md) and the complete
52: [model-visible submission example](../templates/submission-example.md). The
53: example explains metadata placeholders and local-witness accounting; it is not
54: a benchmark or proof certification. Required top-level spec fields are:
55: 
56: - `format_version: 2`, `case_id`, `full_target`, `conclusion` (nonempty strings);
57: - `parameters`: records `{symbol, type}`; parameter symbols reserve global names.
58:   Give ambient data types/structures only. Original conditions, ranges and
59:   equations belong in H, not in parameter refinements that would be visible
60:   to every R;
61: - `hypotheses`: records `{id: Hddd, statement, origin}` extracted before authoring;
62: - `definitions`: records `{id: Dddd, symbol, definition, type, depends_on,
63:   requires, binders, objects}`. Each symbol has exactly one global meaning. `depends_on` lists
64:   earlier/resolvable D IDs and is acyclic. `requires` lists proved H/N IDs that
65:   must already be available whenever the definition is used;
66: - `logic`: `{classical: boolean, rules: [names], calculations: [fixed IDs],
67:   primitives: [{symbol, type, meaning}]}`. In the clean author tool, omit
68:   `calculations` and `primitives` to bind the controller's fixed language profile.
69:   Optional calculation IDs are `equality`, `definitions`, `finite_algebra`,
70:   `finite_order`, `finite_sums`. Optional primitive selections may be
71:   `{symbol: ...}`; the controller validates selections and binds the complete
72:   core syntax with exact type/meaning (numerals, number systems and empty-set/top
73:   notation). This is not a subject vocabulary or a list of allowed theorems. A new
74:   Audit A requires the bound metadata. Author-defined permission descriptions
75:   and conflicting primitive meanings are rejected, not silently accepted;
76: - `pins`: `{lean_version, mathlib_commit, mathlib_root}`; the root is a local
77:   locator, the version/commit are scientific identifiers;
78: - `inputs`: evidence records `{path, sha256}` for the original problem/proof.
79: 
80: The exact machine identifiers permitted in `logic.rules` and inference `rules`
81: are `direct`, `modus_ponens`, `implication_introduction`, `negation_introduction`,
82: `contradiction_classical`, `case_elimination`, `forall_introduction`,
83: `exists_elimination`, and `natural_induction`. Describe algebra/analysis in the
84: actual proof text; it is not a new trusted logical rule. These identifiers
85: describe proof packaging, not a substitute for establishing the implication.
86: 
87: The `elementary-language-4` profile in `nl0/scripts/foundations.py` permits
88: displayed finite algebra/order calculations and ordinary logic. Its core syntax
89: contains no domain-specific vocabulary. Objects and notation from any subject
90: are parameters, D definitions or scoped locals, with explicit meaning, type and
91: dependencies; they cannot be hidden in primitives. Recognizable notation grants
92: no identity, existence or regularity. No global dictionary extension is needed
93: to represent a new subject.
94: For every substantive fact still register an E/M input or give its local proof.
95: 
96: Older saved specifications retain their original bytes and symbol metadata for
97: read-only inspection under their recorded runtime. Starting a new Audit A under
98: this profile requires current canonical metadata: remove obsolete domain
99: primitive entries, declare any objects they actually supplied, and validate
100: the resulting source again. A new profile does not upgrade an old receipt.
101: 
102: Definitions may be globally visible but guarded. Example: “K is the unique
103: fixed curve from N008” requires N008 before K is used. N008 itself must state
104: existence using the previously defined space/operator, without assuming K.
105: Proof prerequisites must be direct inference inputs in v2;
106: the output being proved cannot discharge its own definition prerequisite.
107: Definition prerequisites of input/output statements are checked too.
108: 
109: ## Proposition fields
110: 
111: Every proposition has `id`, `kind`, the complete `statement`, `definitions`
112: (D IDs), `binders`, and `objects`:
113: 
114: - `binders`: `{symbol, type}` records for statement-bound variables. These do
115:   not introduce free variables in a consuming R. Register actual nested scope
116:   in the statement; alpha-rename to avoid global shadowing.
117: - `objects`: distinct names of mathematical objects actually used in the
118:   statement, from frozen parameters/primitives, referenced D closure or these
119:   binders. A D also has these fields for its defining expression.
120: 
121: These are inventories, not a parser-generated list. Audit A must find omitted
122: objects by reading actual prose/formulas. Export all formulas and conditions;
123: another N ID or an original equation number cannot replace their content.
124: 
125: | kind | ID | Producer | Additional fields |
126: |---|---|---|---|
127: | `hypothesis` | Hddd | none | exactly matches frozen H statement |
128: | `mathlib` | Mddd | none | `source` record below |
129: | `external` | Eddd | none | `source` record below |
130: | `internal` | Nddd | exactly one | `origin` locating source or explaining added bridge |
131: | `target` | P | exactly one | exact frozen `conclusion` |
132: 
133: A source record contains `statement` (exact NL restatement), `evidence` (file
134: hashes), and `hypotheses` (complete applicability obligations, not their proof).
135: M additionally has `declaration`, `module`, `mathlib_commit`, `source_path`,
136: `source_sha256`, `signature` (complete Lean output), and `declaration_kind` equal
137: to `theorem` or `proved_instance`. A definition/opaque constant is not a proved
138: source proposition. Library definitions belong in D. A named M's official
139: library dependencies need not be copied into the project graph; pin the library
140: and inspect relevant axioms. Do not introduce project results as library M.
141: M evidence includes the successful version-1 report from `probe_mathlib.py`,
142: with the same ID, declaration, full signature, source bytes and toolchain pins.
143: In the clean Yui NL0 carrier, `probe_library` produces this evidence and the
144: submission adapter binds exact signature/source metadata from the successful
145: probe matching the selected M ID and actual declaration selector. Those metadata
146: fields may be omitted from that tool's submitted JSON; canonical graph files
147: still contain them in full. No unprobed source is filled from model memory.
148: The clean probe resolves genuine aliases to their canonical kernel name and
149: discovers the actual defining module. A requested module is only a locator
150: hint; its correction is recorded, never silently treated as source evidence.
151: Native type printing (and the legacy `#check @declaration` probe) preserves the complete outer telescope,
152: including implicit/typeclass conditions, using ordinary notation for nested
153: structure applications. Recursive expansion of inherited structure arguments
154: is unnecessary; omitted hypotheses or ellipsis are not permitted. The actual
155: kernel declaration kind, axioms, source bytes and version pins remain evidence.
156: For a local development revision the same tool also accepts
157: `{base_input: "declared-task-ID.json", patches: [...]}` when that explicit frozen
158: task document contains `{spec, graph}`. Patches are JSON data operations
159: `add`, `remove`, `replace`, or `test`, each with an absolute JSON pointer inside
160: `/spec/...` or `/graph/...` and a `value` except for `remove`. Array append uses
161: `/-`. An additional `replace_text` operation has `path`, `old` and `new`
162: instead of `value`: it replaces exactly one nonempty literal occurrence inside
163: an existing string. Missing or ambiguous matches are rejected; this is not a
164: regular expression or executable code. It preserves the rest of a long proof
165: paragraph without asking the model to retype it.
166: Every submission starts from the immutable named input, not the previous
167: failed candidate. The controller records the base hash and actual edits, then
168: performs the identical full source/structure checks. Successful output is still
169: the complete canonical `{spec,graph}`. This is an authoring convenience for
170: unaccepted candidates, not an incremental Audit A receipt or permission to
171: modify accepted/frozen source during a translation run. Actual mathematical
172: changes still invalidate affected reviews.
173: Within the same authoring stage, an actual check also returns its
174: `candidate_number`. Use `{base_candidate: N, patches: [...]}` to revise that
175: exact checked draft, including a structurally rejected draft. `read_draft`
176: can inspect a narrow JSON pointer in that own draft. These are the model's
177: own prior submissions plus bound metadata, not other tasks or local files.
178: Every edit still undergoes the full checker, and no draft inherits acceptance.
179: Resubmit an exact own draft with `{accept_candidate: N}` after a successful
180: check. Once a same-stage draft exists, returning to `base_input` requires an
181: explicit `reset_base: true`; this deliberately discards accumulated edits.
182: Without that explicit reset, use `base_candidate` so a later bookkeeping fix
183: cannot silently discard earlier mathematical corrections.
184: The adapter does not rewrite mathematical statements, hypotheses, definitions,
185: binders or arguments. Their fidelity remains the author's and auditor's work.
186: The following two explicit serialization forms copy the author's declared
187: data; they do not infer mathematics or grant Audit A acceptance:
188: 
189: - An S `text`, D `definition`, or `spec.hypotheses[i].statement` may be `{from_task: "declared-input-ID", start_line: 10,
190:   end_line: 20}`. The controller copies exactly those inclusive lines of the
191:   already frozen same-stage input into an ordinary canonical string. It stores
192:   input/text hashes, the exact range and the canonical destination pointer.
193:   Only these proof/definition/hypothesis text fields have this form;
194:   undeclared files, other tasks and old candidates are not source IDs. Read the
195:   materialized draft, normalize source labels to legitimate input/F references,
196:   supply declarations/conditions and retain the complete argument. Copying the
197:   original proof does not establish closed-premise sufficiency. A copied
198:   definition still needs its complete declarations, dependencies and guards;
199:   it grants no mathematical property. A copied H must be a complete original
200:   GIVEN, with its origin retained; copying a desired conclusion or a claim
201:   from the proof does not make it a permissible hypothesis.
202: - `{base_candidate: N, source_uses: [{inference: "R001", at: "S001",
203:   input: "M001", bindings: "actual substitution", hypothesis_checks: [...]}]}`
204:   records existing M/E calls selected explicitly by the author. Each call adds
205:   its ID to that R's `inputs` and S's `uses`, and writes the supplied application
206:   record. Optional `id: Addd` distinguishes actual uses and is required for E.
207:   Exact replay is idempotent; a conflicting existing application must be
208:   explicitly patched. No new proposition/source or proof text is generated.
209:   Every normal check and actual Audit A still runs, including whether the
210:   theorem is actually used and each condition really follows from the packet.

1: # Ordered retrieval of external theorem sources
2: 
3: Use this procedure for each literature E whose original text is missing. Both
4: the NL0 author and global Audit A reviewer follow it. Reuse an already supplied,
5: hash-bound primary document instead of downloading it again. The invoking agent
6: may retrieve sources before dispatch, but every supplied document must be an
7: explicit input; never insert files into an active run's frozen inputs.
8: 
9: ## 1. Identify the requested work and edition
10: 
11: Read the actual citation and its use in the supplied proof. Record author,
12: title, known arXiv ID/version or DOI, source kind, and expected theorem/lemma,
13: page or equation. Search terms must come from that material. Do not invent an
14: identifier or accept a nearby search hit. A shared title does not establish
15: that two editions have the same statements or numbering.
16: 
17: ## 2. Try arXiv first
18: 
19: Call `search_external_sources(query=title_and_authors, engine="arxiv")`. If an
20: arXiv ID is already given, use that exact ID, including its version suffix.
21: Read the matching abstract/version record, then use `read_external_source` on
22: the actual PDF link. The search tool exposes PDF locators from arXiv abstract
23: links; those locators are not a substitute for downloading the PDF.
24: 
25: Check identity, version, page count and the complete relevant result. Follow
26: its definitions and standing hypotheses. If only another version is available,
27: compare the relevant statements and their conventions, or continue searching
28: for the cited edition. Never copy a page number from a different version.
29: Stop retrieval when an adequate original has actually been obtained.
30: 
31: ## 3. Search Google for the complete text
32: 
33: If the needed original is still missing, call
34: `search_external_sources(query=title_and_authors, engine="google")`. Open
35: plausible author, institution, repository or publisher links and download the
36: full document with `read_external_source`. A title-only result, catalog,
37: abstract, search snippet or AI overview does not verify an external theorem.
38: 
39: For `BROWSER_REQUIRED` or a verification page, retry the same search/read with
40: `browser=true`. The controller can use an installed, isolated local Chrome
41: through the fixed optional helper. It performs real navigation and rendered
42: readback, preserves screenshots and uses no personal browser profile. This
43: also works for CLI stages without a desktop tab-control tool. Missing browser
44: dependencies, unresolved challenges and browser failures are explicit records;
45: they do not stop the mathematical workflow by themselves.
46: 
47: An invoking agent with an actual built-in-browser control tool may instead use
48: that frontend and stage the downloaded original before dispatch. Opening or
49: queuing a tab alone is never readback evidence. Do not claim that a headless
50: Chrome session is the user's visible in-app tab.
51: 
52: ## 4. Find and confirm a DOI, then try Sci-Hub
53: 
54: When full text remains missing, search Google again using the exact title,
55: authors and `DOI`. Inspect `doi_candidates` and the linked publisher or DOI
56: metadata; confirm title, author and edition. These strings are only candidate
57: identifiers. Reuse a DOI already established by the supplied bibliography or
58: matching primary metadata; a blocked Google page need not prevent that lookup.
59: Do not guess a DOI or request an unrelated article just to make retrieval pass.
60: 
61: Call `search_external_sources(query=confirmed_doi, engine="scihub", browser=true)`.
62: The controller navigates to `https://sci-hub.box/<DOI>`. Ordinary site controls,
63: including its own ALTCHA verification button when present, may complete normal
64: access. Follow the returned PDF/object link through `read_external_source`.
65: Record any redirect, including a different mirror's final hostname, rather
66: than claiming the bytes came from the initial host. Do not fabricate challenge
67: tokens, import personal cookies, silently purchase access or change system
68: proxy settings. If a challenge cannot be completed normally, retain the failure
69: and move to the disclosed conditional route.
70: 
71: ## 5. Establish source fidelity after retrieval
72: 
73: Retain the actual URL, final URL, retrieval timestamp, document/text hashes and
74: access receipt. A fetched PDF is a readable source candidate, not an automatic
75: truth or theorem-fidelity judgment. Apply [external-theorem review](external-theorems.md):
76: confirm author/title/version, locate the result, read the full statement and
77: governing definitions, check corrections/version history where available, and
78: map every hypothesis, conclusion and constant dependency to E. Each application
79: still needs its own verified substitutions and premise checks. A source that
80: states a different theorem is a mismatch, not an inaccessible-text deferral.
81: 
82: For a changed edition, retain both document hashes and a locator/statement map.
83: Do not silently substitute the journal version for a cited preprint. Any
84: substantive normalization bridge belongs in an internal proved node.
85: 
86: ## 6. Record unavailable verification and continue
87: 
88: After actual unsuccessful retrieval, follow [conditional sources](conditional-sources.md).
89: Supply `defer_primary_source` with the E ID, a complete exact quotation already
90: present in a declared secondary input, its input ID and own failed
91: `access_records` paths. An unavailable original does not justify inventing a
92: statement from memory or treating a known contradiction as an assumption.
93: If the statement itself is missing or incomplete, identify that missing content
94: instead of pretending the source-only route closes the proof.
95: 
96: Retain `UNVERIFIED_PRIMARY`, `warn.json` and `warn.md`. Continue all other
97: mathematical, Lean, assembly and audit work normally. The final result remains
98: `WORKFLOW-CONDITIONAL` (or the corresponding stage's conditional status) until
99: the actual source and affected review are completed. Display each warning to
100: the user when it arises and in the final answer. A compile pass does not remove
101: source uncertainty. Do not repeat indefinitely an unchanged blocked query;
102: preserve its failure and advance to the next route.
103: 
104: ## Optional local browser setup
105: 
106: No browser package is installed automatically. `nl0/scripts/source_browser.py`
107: looks for Node on PATH or the bundled Codex runtime, its bundled Playwright,
108: and an installed Chrome/Chromium. Other installations can set:
109: 
110: ```sh
111: export YUI_SOURCE_BROWSER_NODE="/absolute/path/to/node"
112: export YUI_SOURCE_BROWSER_MODULE="/absolute/path/to/playwright/index.mjs"
113: export YUI_SOURCE_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE="/absolute/path/to/chrome"
114: ```
115: 
116: These select existing host tools, not model-generated commands or scripts. An
117: invalid explicit override is reported without silently choosing another tool.
118: The trusted driver is included in frozen runtime hashes. Each call owns its
119: temporary Chrome profile and process group; cancellation and a transport wait
120: timeout close those processes. The wait timeout is a browser operation limit,
121: not a case/proof budget. Source readback keeps the existing 32 MiB file limit.
122: An unavailable browser leaves ordinary HTTPS and conditional continuation usable.

1: # Self-containment details
2: 
3: This details the statement/object and dependency/scope requirements grouped
4: under Audit A's statement_closure and dependency_closure criteria. The
5: [shared Audit A section](audit-a.md#shared-mathematical-acceptance-requirements)
6: is the acceptance authority for author and auditor; this annex supplies
7: interpretation and examples, not an independent permission policy.
8: 
9: ## Two boundaries
10: 
11: Accepted NL0 is a complete proof relative to its declared H/E/M roots, frozen
12: logical foundation and version-bound mathematically reviewed background notes. It is not an outline requiring the original manuscript to
13: recover missing definitions, formulas, assumptions, or arguments. E/M statements
14: are fully restated; their primary sources are inspected for provenance, not
15: used to supply unstated premises. The fixed library's own proof dependencies
16: need not be recopied. The target work's internal results must be proved here.
17: 
18: Every R must also be checkable from its packet alone: the complete statements
19: of its direct inputs, their required definitions/declarations, its complete
20: output, its local declarations, and its own argument. Another R's proof body,
21: an ancestor not listed as an input, an ambient original H, an original-source
22: crosswalk, or remembered material is not an additional mathematical resource.
23: Whole-target/source-fidelity checks are separate from this local proof check.
24: Under mathematical-background-v2-1, a reviewer may positively assess routine
25: local mathematical facts and record precise statements, available conditions
26: and justification. Exact Mathlib bindings are deferred to nl02lean; no native
27: query is required for ordinary background. These notes add neither H nor a
28: core proof route. Mathematical uncertainty still blocks. See
29: [background notes](background-notes.md).
30: 
31: Original theorem conditions are H nodes, including conditions that could be
32: encoded in a refined type. Parameters introduce ambient data/structures, not
33: an ambient stock of original hypotheses. For example, declare a vector and
34: put its required nonzero condition in H; do not write “nonzero vector” in its
35: parameter type and use that condition from an empty input list. The same rule
36: applies to characteristic/range conditions and equations. An R must list every
37: original H it actually uses. Standard structure operations/axioms and the fixed
38: finite-language rules remain available; no new substantive theorem is added.
39: 
40: An output must be understandable and callable without reading its producer's
41: argument. Include the actual equalities/inequalities, binder types, hypotheses,
42: parameter windows, constant dependencies, representatives and a.e./pointwise
43: meaning. Global defined notation can be expanded from the packet. A formula
44: number, theorem name, or paragraph location cannot replace mathematical content.
45: Source locators belong in provenance fields. New mathematical prose uses direct
46: input IDs and previously proved local F IDs, not inherited numbered references.
47: 
48: ## Object closure
49: 
50: For every mathematical object actually appearing in a statement, definition,
51: local declaration, or proof, locate one legitimate declaration:
52: 
53: 1. A frozen parameter, explicit logical primitive, or global D definition.
54:    State its meaning, type/domain and parameter dependence. Global primitives
55:    cover only core typed syntax, not a dictionary of subject-specific objects.
56:    New subjects use the same parameter/definition/local declaration mechanism;
57:    symbol registration never licenses a theorem.
58: 2. A binder inside the current proposition's full statement. Its scope remains
59:    that statement. A variable bound in an input does not become a free object
60:    in the consuming proof; instantiate the statement explicitly.
61: 3. A local declaration before first use, recording its kind, type, exact
62:    declaration, introduction basis, and scope. An arbitrary variable requires
63:    legitimate quantifier introduction; a definition uses already available
64:    objects; a witness requires an input or an earlier local existence proof.
65: 
66: A declaration cannot grant existence, uniqueness, invertibility, regularity,
67: or a desired property merely by naming an object. Those obligations require
68: proof. Any D guard needed to use the object must be a direct R input, not a
69: theorem silently recovered from ancestor closure. Record mutually compatible
70: choices and witness dependence. Temporary assumptions stay inside R and must
71: be correctly discharged. Branch witnesses, local facts and local notation
72: cannot escape their scopes. Export a quantified or conditional statement when
73: needed, rather than a free private name. Global names are reserved; dummy
74: variables may be reused in disjoint local scopes.
75: 
76: ## Dependency closure
77: 
78: Inventory actual factual uses from the prose back to their grounds, not just
79: from an input list forward to a generic `uses` list. Each substantive imported theorem, prior project lemma or original
80: assumption must be a direct input. Eligible routine mathematical facts are recorded as mathematical audit notes
81: with actual local grounds, without requiring a native implementation lookup. A definition supplies meaning, not a theorem. An R output is not its
82: own premise. Adding the desired formula as an unproved input is not a repair.
83: 
84: Explicit local calculations and fully proved intermediate facts may remain
85: inside R. Give a reused local fact a full F statement and identify its earlier
86: derivation and open assumptions. No separate graph vertex is needed for every
87: algebraic equality. A nontrivial imported result cannot be called a local
88: calculation. Substantive reusable lemmas should become N/R pairs; any fact
89: reused by another R must be exported in a complete proposition statement.
90: 
91: The controller owns `spec.logic.calculations` and the small core syntax table
92: (`nl0/scripts/foundations.py`). The clean author tool binds omitted metadata and
93: rejects extra author permissions or task-specific primitives. This fixed
94: language grants no MVT, FTC, Fubini, convergence, compactness or regularity
95: theorem. Such facts need legitimate explicit inputs, an actual local derivation or
96: eligible positively reviewed mathematical background; the syntax table alone
97: grants none of them.
98: An author-written permission claim, in any field or prose, has no authority.
99: Ordinary typed arithmetic notation is part of this fixed language: natural
100: numbers, integers, rationals, reals and complex numbers mean their standard
101: structures with usual numerals and operations. Finite calculations include
102: their zero/one laws, such as `a+0=a`, as well as explicit algebra/order
103: derivations. Do not demand a separate E/M for an operation token or an allowed
104: finite calculation. This does not grant calculus, topology or measure theorems.
105: Conversely, inspect an actual displayed local derivation before demanding a
106: duplicate E/M input for its conclusion. A named consequence proved by permitted
107: finite algebra/order steps is not an imported premise. If a local derivation
108: fails, locate its unsupported implication rather than its absent theorem name.
109: 
110: Metadata accounts for the argument but never replaces it. Copying all inputs
111: into a single `uses` record, registering a symbol without declaring it in the
112: proof, or writing a PASS label cannot establish closure.
113: 
114: ## Operational acceptance
115: 
116: 1. Author using the node template. Reverse-check the actual prose for missing
117:    declarations, unexpanded references and unlisted facts before freezing.
118: 2. Generate a packet for each R. The v2 generator supplies no original proof,
119:    producer proofs, provenance file locators, extra ancestor statements or
120:    undeclared ambient H. Direct source contracts and required definitions are
121:    included. Packet hashes bind the mathematical input actually reviewed.
122: 3. Review all closure/inference checks, admitting positively checked routine
123:    background notes under the shared policy. Record concrete packet locations and reasons for every verdict.
124: 4. Perform a fresh local mathematical replay. The reviewer gets the skill instructions
125:    and that packet, without original proof,
126:    other R bodies, author review
127:    notes, old verdicts, or an answer key. Record the actual carrier, packet hash,
128:    prior exposure and mathematical material read. Skill instructions supply no
129:    extra mathematical premise. Do not falsely claim a same-context rereading
130:    is a fresh replay. This rule does not authorize starting a new external
131:    service or agent; if the required carrier has not been used, keep replay
132:    UNVERIFIED and report that limit.
133:    Prior exposure means known task/proof material supplied or read in earlier
134:    contexts; this is not a claim about unknown pretraining contents. Learned
135:    mathematical knowledge cannot replace a missing declared premise or proof.
136: 5. An ineligible missing declaration, missing statement content, unlisted substantive theorem or need
137:    to look outside the packet blocks acceptance. Record the defect; do not
138:    silently repair it while assigning PASS. Return substantive/structural defects to authoring and review the frozen
139:    revision; eligible background notes need no author rewrite. Routine completion does not require a
140:    separate user interruption for every omission. Distinguish a representation
141:    defect from a substantive mathematical gap under the existing gap policy.
142: 
143: The code rejects explicit malformed references, inventories, scopes, guards
144: and receipts. It does not infer hidden hypotheses from property words in types,
145: or decide theorem applications by matching a list of mathematical names.
146: These semantic obligations apply equally to every subject and remain part of
147: author inspection and Audit A. An omitted inventory entry or unnamed
148: theorem hidden in prose still requires actual semantic review. Freshness and
149: truthful reviewer identity need execution evidence; record shape/hashes cannot
150: authenticate them. No natural-language audit is a Lean kernel certificate.

211: 
212: To avoid retranscribing mandatory duplicate strings, its tool input may omit
213: an H node's `statement` (copied from the same artifact's `spec.hypotheses`),
214: P's `statement` (copied from `spec.conclusion`), or an E/M `source.statement`
215: (copied from that proposition's primary `statement`). This is serialization of
216: one authoritative text, not a second premise or an inferred theorem. Canonical
217: files contain all fields. Conflicting supplied duplicates are rejected with
218: both texts shown; they are never silently overwritten. The actual external
219: `source_statement` and the probed Lean signature remain separate source-fidelity
220: evidence that Audit A must compare to the primary project restatement.
221: Use a fresh probe output directory for a new source-query version. The helper
222: refuses to overwrite existing evidence; `--replace-existing` deliberately
223: archives previous outputs and revokes the old active receipt before rerunning.
224: The checker verifies this record binding; it does not authenticate a fabricated
225: execution transcript. Audit A still reads the actual source and checks meaning.
226: 
227: E additionally has nonempty strings `author`, `title`, `version`, `identifier`,
228: `locator`, `notation_map`, `errata`, `source_kind`, `origin`, `retrieved_at`,
229: `source_statement`, `context`, `qualification`, and `version_check`, plus
230: `primary_evidence`: a nonempty list of hashed evidence records also present in
231: `evidence`. `source_statement` records the actual source theorem and its full
232: conditions, separately from the project's restatement. `version_check` states
233: the check date, scope, findings and effect; `qualification` explains source
234: category and proved-result eligibility. Read the full
235: [external-theorem review standard](external-theorems.md).
236: The explicit [conditional-source route](conditional-sources.md) additionally
237: allows `verification: {status: "UNVERIFIED_PRIMARY", record: {path, sha256}}`.
238: Only with that validated record may `primary_evidence` be empty. The record
239: binds the exact complete secondary statement and actual failed retrievals;
240: Audit A remains source-unverified and the final workflow stays conditional.
241: A DOI/URL alone is insufficient. Include an
242: accessible local primary document and precise excerpt/location evidence. Do not call
243: the target work's unproved internal lemma an imported E. Existing internally
244: proved modules need a separate expanded graph or a versioned proof handoff;
245: version 2 does not silently certify an opaque module.
246: 
247: Every retained non-H proposition must be in P's backward dependency closure.
248: Every frozen H is present as an initial graph node, including an unused H.
249: Report unused H rather than removing it or changing the original statement.
250: 
251: ## Inference fields
252: 
253: Required fields: `id: Rddd`, `inputs` (unique proposition IDs), `output` (one
254: N/P ID), `definitions` (direct D references), `rules` (permitted logic-rule
255: names), `locals`, `argument`, and `applications`.
256: 
257: - `locals`: `{symbol, type, scope}` records. Scope identifies a binding inside
258:   this inference; names cannot shadow globals. Two bindings in different
259:   scopes/nodes may use the same spelling. Bound variables of source theorems
260:   can be alpha-renamed and instantiated. Audit actual binding/freshness.
261:   In v2 also require `start`, `end` (inclusive S IDs), `kind` (`arbitrary`,
262:   `definition`, or `witness`), `declaration` (full introduction), `from_inputs`,
263:   `from_local` (prior F IDs) and `objects` (already available objects used to
264:   introduce this one). A witness must have an input/local existence basis.
265:   The checker verifies declared availability/order, not the existence claim's
266:   semantics. Source-bound variables need a legitimate local instantiation.
267:   The `scope` label and inclusive start/end must agree with the prose. Keep an
268:   object live through its last actual use. Establish an existence F in an
269:   earlier S, then choose its witness in a subsequent S; using a newly produced
270:   F as the witness basis in the same paragraph is a forward reference.
271: - `argument`: ordered records `{id: Sddd, text, uses, uses_local, objects,
272:   produces, introduces, discharges}`. S IDs are inference-local and unique. `uses`
273:   lists direct graph inputs used at this point. Local facts established earlier
274:   in the prose do not become graph inputs. The union of `uses` must equal
275:   `inputs`. A citation's presence is not semantic evidence that it was used.
276:   `uses_local` lists only earlier F IDs; `objects` lists the actually used
277:   global/active local objects. `produces` holds complete local facts
278:   `{id: Fddd, statement, binders, objects, assumptions}`; assumptions lists remaining
279:   local L IDs on which the fact depends. A local fact cannot be used before
280:   its production or outside its assumption/object scope. A paragraph cannot
281:   cite its newly produced F as a previous premise. Formulas to be reused by a
282:   different R must appear in the exported proposition, not only in `produces`.
283: - `introduces`/`discharges`: lists of inference-local assumption IDs (e.g.
284:   `L1`). Temporary assumptions are never proposition vertices. Every introduced
285:   ID is unique in this inference and must be discharged once, no earlier than
286:   introduction. These lists account for prose; Audit A checks the actual
287:   formula, scope, and chosen rule. A correctly closed implication may retain
288:   the assumption in its antecedent. Deleting the ID cannot justify an output.
289: - `applications`: records covering every directly used E/M input, with
290:   `{input, at: Sddd, bindings, hypothesis_checks}`.
291:   `bindings` is a nonempty string spelling out the actual variable/parameter
292:   substitution; it is not a JSON mapping. `hypothesis_checks` is an ordered
293:   list of nonempty strings, one per declared source obligation. For example,
294:   `"bindings": "Set the source parameter a to the current x."` records a
295:   substitution; it does not prove its conditions.
296:   The S paragraph must list
297:   this input in `uses`; only local facts available before that paragraph may
298:   supply application conditions. E applications additionally require
299:   an inference-local unique `id: Addd`; different actual uses of the same E
300:   need separate IDs and records. M may also use explicit A IDs for repeated
301:   instances; a legacy M without `id` uses its input ID as the unique key.
302:   `hypothesis_checks` has one nonempty
303:   explanation for each corresponding source obligation. A hypothesis needs an
304:   actual argument from inputs/H/local proved facts; filling a string is only
305:   an accounting check. Prove substantive normalization bridges as N nodes.
306: 
307: Input-free R nodes are permitted only for explicitly shown calculations or
308: logical/definitional consequences. They are audited proofs, not a fourth kind
309: of trusted source. Transitive inputs need not be repeated unless used directly.
310: 
311: ## Audit record
312: 
313: `audit-a.json` contains `format_version`, `graph_sha256`, `spec_sha256`,
314: `reviewer` (`identity`, `mode`, `independent`, `disclosure`), `target_review`,
315: `definition_reviews`, `source_reviews`, and `inference_reviews`.
316: 
317: Each review contains `verdict: PASS|FAIL|UNVERIFIED`, substantive `notes`, and
318: hashed `evidence`. Yui inference reviews contain five grouped check review objects:
319: `statement_closure`, `dependency_closure`, `argument`, `applicability`,
320: `packet_replay`. Object scope and exact output correctness remain required
321: inside these grouped mathematical assessments.
322: Each check has `{verdict, notes, evidence, locations}`. `locations` contains
323: JSON pointers resolving inside that R's actual packet, such as
324: `/inputs/0/statement` or `/inference/argument/1/text`. PASS requires at least
325: one actual inspected location; a boolean/enum alone is insufficient.
326: Every D, every E/M source, every R, and the target must be covered exactly once.
327: Spec input hashes and source evidence are read back; malformed/duplicate JSON
328: keys, missing files, changed bytes, failed verdicts, and stale audit hashes fail.
329: 
330: Use audit `format_version: 4` for all new Yui records. A detailed-NL0 audit v3
331: cannot establish format-4 acceptance. Historical audit v1/v2 remains inspectable only
332: with historical graph v1 and --legacy, never as current acceptance.
333: Each E source review additionally has `citation_checks`, mapping exactly
334: `literature_identity`, `result_location`, `statement_fidelity`,
335: `context_completeness`, `version_and_eligibility` to separate ordinary review
336: objects `{verdict, notes, evidence}`.
337: Each version-4 inference review additionally has `external_applications`,
338: mapping exactly its E application A IDs to records
339: `{input, verdict, notes, evidence, bindings_review, hypothesis_reviews,
340: conclusion_review, bridges}`. `input` must match A's E; each nested review
341: has `{verdict, notes, evidence}`; the ordered `hypothesis_reviews` list matches
342: all source obligations one for one. `bridges` lists N nodes already in R's
343: direct input list. A bridge string is not a proof of that bridge.
344: 
345: Each inference review also has `replay: {packet_sha256, mode, carrier,
346: prior_exposure, read_materials}`. Modes are `unperformed`,
347: `same_context_diagnostic`, and `fresh_packet_only`. A passing replay/overall
348: inference requires the actual fresh carrier, empty prior proof exposure, and
349: `read_materials` equal to `["packet:<hash>"]` for mathematical input. Skill
350: instructions supply the procedure, not additional mathematics. The hash must
351: match the regenerated packet. Keep traces as evidence; metadata cannot
352: authenticate a claimed identity or prove truthful isolation.
353: 
354: Format 4 may additionally bind `review_trace:{path,sha256}` for actual tool logs.
355: This is execution metadata, not a native theorem source or an extra premise.
356: `library_evidence` contains only the successful pinned evidence of explicitly
357: retained native mathlib notes; ordinary mathematical notes require none.
358: 
359: `audit-template` creates only UNVERIFIED reviews, empty check locations and an
360: unperformed replay. It refuses to overwrite an existing output. It does not
361: inherit author notes or old verdicts. `inspect-audit` can inspect this pending
362: record; `check --audit` rejects it. Each PASS must come from actual review.
363: 
364: `check --audit` accepts only fully passing records. `inspect-audit --audit`
365: also validates the completeness and evidence of FAIL/UNVERIFIED records and
366: returns their unresolved review paths; success of inspection is not proof
367: acceptance. Overall PASS with a failed child review never passes acceptance.
368: 
369: Mode `same_context_self_audit` requires `independent: false`. If claiming an
370: independent review, disclose its actual carrier and input boundary; this file
371: does not authenticate identity or prove independence.
372: 
373: ## Local packet
374: 
375: The v2 packet contains `contract_version`, `case_id`, spec/graph hashes,
376: parameters, fixed logic, pins, expanded definitions, complete input/output
377: ports, the current inference, a warning, and `packet_sha256`. Source ports keep
378: applicability obligations and M signatures; primary-document verification is
379: separate. Producer arguments, original-proof locations, source proof text,
380: non-input H and extra ancestor/guard statements are not supplied. Guards must
381: already be direct inputs. The packet intentionally omits the global full target
382: so that its unstated premises cannot become an ambient local hypothesis.
383: 
384: Its digest is SHA256 of UTF-8 canonical JSON (`sort_keys=True`,
385: `ensure_ascii=False`, `separators=(",", ":")`) excluding `packet_sha256`.
386: It is independent of audit-verdict fields, avoiding a circular receipt hash.
387: Packets are generated views and never a second editable proof authority.
388: 
389: ## Mechanical boundaries
390: 
391: The checker validates declared objects, the frozen contract, graph closure,
392: notation-name metadata, citation parity, local-assumption accounting, guarded
393: definition availability, and hash-bound audit coverage. It verifies source
394: checkout/file hashes, not the truth of a source restatement. The printed
395: signature must be obtained from a successful pinned Lean probe and compared by
396: the auditor; an arbitrary string called `signature` is not verification.
397: 
398: The checker cannot establish that a natural-language formula is well typed,
399: that two spellings have the same mathematical meaning, that a hidden theorem
400: was not used, that a local witness did not escape the prose, or that an argument
401: is valid. Those are explicit Audit A obligations. Neither a JSON PASS nor a
402: fabricated complete audit receipt is a mathematical certificate.
403: Numbered-reference diagnostics reject common opaque references, not every
404: possible paraphrase or hidden import. Behavioral tests must actually ask an
405: auditor to review unseen controls; manually prefilled FAIL records only test
406: receipt rejection and must be reported as such.
407: 
408: ## Mathematical background receipt extension
409: 
410: New receipts declare `background_policy: "mathematical-background-v2-1"`.
411: Each R may contain background_notes with precise mathematics, local grounds and
412: actual justification; native lookup is not required. A new supplemented replay
413: uses fresh_packet_with_mathematical_background. Optional existing native notes
414: retain their complete bound library evidence; mathematical/elementary notes
415: carry no native source claim. The authored graph remains unchanged. Other
416: variant consumers must reject unsupported receipts instead of dropping fields.
417: 
418: `nl0.validate` returns the note supplement/hash and note count. A packet read
419: from an accepted source includes its notes and the original reviewed-packet
420: hash. This enriched view is not claimed to be the original replay input.
421: Translation binds the supplement in `contract.source.background_supplement_sha256`.
422: 
423: The interface source also retains the complete `background_supplement`, not
424: just its hash. Plan steps list the relevant qualified note IDs, for example
425: `background_notes:["R004.BG001"]`. Workflow freeze checks the paragraph mapping;
426: local Lean packets receive only their selected notes.

1: # Audit A: mathematical review in Yui
2: 
3: <!-- yui-nl0-acceptance:begin -->
4: ## Shared mathematical acceptance requirements
5: 
6: Contract version: `yui-nl0-audit-a-2`.
7: 
8: The author and independent auditor use this same mathematical standard. NL0
9: reviews a complete natural-language proof and necessary mathematical detail.
10: Specific Lean declarations, signatures, representations and proof tactics are
11: implementation work for nl02lean, not prerequisites for ordinary NL0 review.
12: The following grouped criteria replace V1's ten separate per-R report rows.
13: 
14: | ID | Review group | Author evidence group | Requirement |
15: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
16: | `target` | package | original_context_note | Preserve the complete original theorem, every original H, quantifier, domain, normalization, parameter range, constant dependency and supplied active proof route. In explicit 2basis mode, the original task remains target/H authority and the basis proof is the authorized active route; review both, including replacements and new derivations. A parameter or definition cannot hide a hypothesis or desired conclusion. |
17: | `definitions` | package | declaration_check | Define mathematical objects and notation sufficiently for their actual uses. Check types, dependencies, construction guards and legitimate local introductions. A definition grants no unproved property. |
18: | `sources` | package | original_context_note | Check complete E statements, primary-source identity, context and conditions under the source policy. An explicitly selected native M retains its bound signature checks; authors need not introduce M nodes for ordinary mathematical background. Unavailable originals remain disclosed UNVERIFIED source assumptions. |
19: | `structure` | package | original_context_note | Verify the actual AND dependency graph, unique producers, absence of cycles and faithful exported statements. Retain every original H and disclose unused H. Internal results are proved, never new roots. |
20: | `statement_closure` | closure | output_notes | Inputs and output state the mathematical content, objects, domains, quantifiers and conditions their consumers need. Check actual object occurrences and definitions. No missing identification can be supplied by an absent producer proof or a paper equation number. |
21: | `dependency_closure` | closure | dependency_and_local_assumption_check | Check direct input use, earlier local facts, witness existence and proper discharge of assumptions. No circular dependency, future fact or escaped local object is allowed. Mathematically checked routine background may supplement the packet without prior native lookup. |
22: | `argument` | inference | dependency_and_local_assumption_check | Verify the complete implication and every output clause at ordinary rigorous mathematical granularity, including material limiting operations, domains and regularity. Compress correct routine reasoning; locate a real gap rather than requiring a transcript of elementary steps. |
23: | `applicability` | inference | source_application_check | Check actual instantiations and all material premises of invoked E/M or routine background facts, with grounds in inputs or earlier local derivations. Required bridges are proved. A familiar theorem name or a proposed Lean tactic supplies no mathematical justification. |
24: 
25: ### Scope and mathematical boundary
26: 
27: Global review owns target/H fidelity, definitions, source statements and graph
28: consistency. Each local reviewer owns the conditional implication at its R
29: node. Conditional packet replay has a different input boundary: these statements are conditional premises.
30: The local reviewer does not re-prove an input N or re-audit its source paper;
31: the graph and that producer's review establish those separate obligations.
32: Conversely, an input N exports only its full statement, not unexported facts
33: from the producer's body. The fifth local criterion, packet_replay, assesses
34: sufficiency under this exact boundary. The controller records execution
35: identity and exposure independently of the mathematical judgment.
36: 
37: Review correctness rather than the number of displayed lines. Ordinary valid
38: textbook compression is allowed. Material missing hypotheses, witnesses,
39: constructions, scope discharges or core arguments are not implementation gaps.
40: Return them for located author repair and fresh review. No theorem needs to be re-proved
41: when its legitimate mathematical source and actual application suffice.
42: 
43: The domain-neutral elementary-language-4 profile retains equality, supplied
44: definitions, finite arithmetic/order reasoning and finite sums. It is syntax
45: and elementary calculation policy, not a subject vocabulary or theorem list.
46: Objects from any field use problem parameters, D definitions or scoped locals.
47: Neither an author-written calculation list nor a familiar symbol adds a theorem.
48: 
49: ### Mathematical background: mathematical-background-v2-1
50: 
51: A reviewer may positively assess a routine, local mathematical fact without
52: first finding its Mathlib declaration. Record its precise mathematical
53: statement, actual argument location, available condition grounds and a short
54: mathematical justification in a background note. Use kind mathematical for an
55: ordinary background result and elementary for a useful elementary completion.
56: This is an actual mathematical judgment, not a future TODO or a claim of
57: native verification. Do not record every algebraic operation.
58: 
59: Eligibility requires a correct standard local step with all premises already
60: available, no new H and no substantial new core proof or changed route.
61: Important external tools remain explicit E inputs; a missing project result
62: or uncertain source cannot be waived as background. If an explicitly supplied
63: native mathlib note is retained, its full bound evidence is still validated.
64: No field-specific whitelist determines eligibility.
65: 
66: The accepted authority is immutable author NL0 plus its hash-bound mathematical
67: review supplement. It is a natural-language audit under the mathematical-background policy, not a
68: detailed-NL0 format-3 native-background receipt. At nl02lean, workers must discharge all necessary
69: facts by actual Lean proofs or checked library use; a note never becomes an
70: unproved H, axiom or extra external assumption. The exact implementation may
71: differ while preserving the mathematical meaning.
72: 
73: ### Actual review and result qualification
74: 
75: Independent reviewers assess the actual content; schema validation does not
76: prove mathematics. An unexamined item remains unread/read. A mathematical
77: uncertainty is assessed UNVERIFIED, not PASS. Missing or conflicting assessments
78: block acceptance. Ordinary source-access deferral follows the conditional-source
79: policy and must appear in final warnings; it cannot yield unqualified PASS.
80: 
81: Use short located reasons for straightforward PASS items and enough detail to
82: make a defect or uncertainty actionable. Avoid duplicate explanations across
83: criteria. A concise report still covers every required mathematical check.
84: Do not read author self-check notes, old verdicts, other R proof bodies, other
85: case results or personal proof skills to manufacture independent approval.
86: <!-- yui-nl0-acceptance:end -->
87: 
88: ## Execution protocol
89: 
90: 1. Freeze the original problem, spec and NL0. A separate fresh global reviewer
91:    reads the exhaustive global-overview.json, relevant canonical content and
92:    source evidence. Review each D and selected E/M; the overview is data, not
93:    an assessment. Do not infer absence from a partial page.
94: 2. Complete global source/graph review before dispatching local R reviews.
95:    Independent R reviewers use the current R-node count as their default slot
96:    limit, or the user's explicit positive N cap.
97:    Each receives only its own packet and mathematical-NL0 rules. Review full arguments,
98:    actual applications and definitions; input N statements are conditional.
99: 3. Prefer one complete artifact with an explicit coverage map. Use
100:    record_review_item and read_review_progress only for useful checkpoints.
101:    record_background_note is optional; a complete artifact may include its
102:    actual notes directly. Batch reading several declared fragments is available.
103: 4. Each local report has inference, packet_sha256, verdict, notes, checks,
104:    findings and optional background_notes. The checks map contains exactly
105:    statement_closure, dependency_closure, argument, applicability, packet_replay.
106:    Each row has verdict, notes and resolving packet locations. E applications
107:    additionally retain actual binding, per-hypothesis, conclusion and bridge
108:    assessments; this is mathematical applicability, not a Lean API inventory.
109: 5. Global reports have target_review, definition_reviews, source_reviews,
110:    structure_review and findings. Each E adds citation_checks for
111:    literature_identity, result_location, statement_fidelity,
112:    context_completeness, version_and_eligibility. Inaccessible primary text
113:    leaves blocked checks UNVERIFIED while remaining assessment continues.
114: 6. A blocking finding needs its actual location, explanation and a short exact
115:    quotation from that location. Preserve the defect and untouched coverage.
116:    Return located mathematical repairs to the author; review changed scopes
117:    independently. Do not resample a mathematical rejection or silently erase it.
118: 7. The collector checks complete coverage, consistency, exact bytes and actual
119:    independent execution before producing the audit-format-4 receipt.
120:    Old detailed-NL0 format-3 receipts are not silently upgraded. Inherited format-4 judgments retain
121:    their original source/rule hashes, exposure and costs.
122: 
123: ## Sources, scopes and final handoff
124: 
125: Use [external theorem review](external-theorems.md) and
126: [conditional sources](conditional-sources.md) for source identity, exact
127: statements and warnings. Reuse adequate original text; several theorem uses
128: may share one staged readback. Each application still discharges its own
129: premises. No successful download or guessed Mathlib availability is approval.
130: 
131: Use [logical rules](logical-rules.md) for local scopes and
132: [background notes](background-notes.md) for the mathematical supplement.
133: The ordinary complete result remains relative to explicit E assumptions.
134: An inaccessible E original permits only a source-qualified result. Translation
135: retains this exact audit and supplement until reviewed mathematical changes
136: invalidate affected scopes. Typed interfaces, native checking, standalone
137: assembly and independent semantic Audit B are separate later gates.
138: 
139: ## Paywalled or inaccessible primary text
140: 
141: Follow [conditional sources](conditional-sources.md). Preserve the complete
142: secondary statement and actual access evidence; unavailable source checks
143: stay UNVERIFIED. Continue other work only with an explicitly qualified source
144: assumption, and report warn.json/warn.md. No unqualified full PASS is granted.

1: # NL0 and Audit A stage
2: 
3: This is stage one of Yui. It may be used independently, or its accepted artifacts may feed the translation stage. Existing production skills and historical proof verdicts are not imported by invoking Yui.
4: 
5: ## Required reading
6: 
7: Read [the data contract](nl0-format.md),
8: [self-containment requirements](self-containment.md),
9: [authoring instructions](nl0-authoring.md), and
10: [Audit A](audit-a.md) before building or accepting an NL0.
11: For conditional proofs, contradiction, cases, quantifiers, or induction also
12: read [logical packaging](logical-rules.md).
13: Read [the Lean handoff boundary](lean-handoff.md) only when preparing
14: a formalization handoff. None of these documents automatically dispatches
15: another agent or authorizes an external service.
16: 
17: ## Shared standard and execution responsibilities
18: 
19: [Audit A's shared mathematical requirements](audit-a.md#shared-mathematical-acceptance-requirements)
20: are the single acceptance authority. Their stable IDs bind the author guide,
21: author inspection groups and mathematical audit checks. The clean author and
22: Audit A receive the same frozen section/version/hash directly. The format and
23: self-containment documents supply schemas and detailed meanings; they do not
24: expand the trusted elementary layer.
25: 
26: Author the frozen original problem using the [construction guide](nl0-authoring.md)
27: and [tool template](../templates/authoring.md). Build the actual proof,
28: declarations, source contracts and input/output interfaces together. Preserve
29: routine completion and substantive-gap handling in that guide.
30: 
31: At release, inspect the stored own packets and report actual readiness. Keep
32: known unresolved findings open until their located correction or justified
33: withdrawal. Complete notes alone do not finish authoring. An unfinished draft
34: is preserved as unfinished, without an ordinary first-acceptance audit.
35: 
36: The auditor separately performs the execution protocol in Audit A: source
37: verification, global review, fresh packet-only replay, actual judgments and
38: recorded evidence. Authors do not generate those verdicts. The NL0 author and
39: global Audit A are serial. After the global stage, independent frozen R packets
40: are reviewed with one slot per current R node by default, or the explicit N cap.
41: Separate cases can run concurrently.
42: 
43: ## Execute
44: 
45: Keep `spec.json` independent of the authoring file. The canonical proof is
46: `nl0.json`; `NL0.md` and `graph.mmd` are generated views. Do not edit the views
47: as mathematical authorities.
48: 
49: ```bash
50: python3 nl0/scripts/nl0.py check PATH/nl0.json --spec PATH/spec.json
51: python3 nl0/scripts/nl0.py render PATH/nl0.json --spec PATH/spec.json --out PATH/views
52: python3 nl0/scripts/nl0.py packet PATH/nl0.json --spec PATH/spec.json --inference R001
53: python3 nl0/scripts/nl0.py audit-template PATH/nl0.json --spec PATH/spec.json --out PATH/audit-a.json
54: python3 nl0/scripts/nl0.py check PATH/nl0.json --spec PATH/spec.json --audit PATH/audit-a.json
55: python3 nl0/scripts/nl0.py inspect-audit PATH/nl0.json --spec PATH/spec.json --audit PATH/audit-a.json
56: ```
57: 
58: Commands print JSON and return nonzero on a failed gate. `inspect-audit` may
59: successfully validate the completeness of a FAIL/UNVERIFIED record; its
60: `audit_receipt_valid` remains false and it is never an acceptance command.
61: The executable format
62: and exact meaning of the checks are documented in the data contract. Programs
63: validate explicit metadata and evidence binding; they cannot recognize every
64: undeclared theorem or prove a natural-language argument.
65: 
66: New spec/graph files use format v2 and mathematical-NL0 audits use v4.
67: A detailed-NL0 audit v3 does not establish current format-4 acceptance. Historical v1 files
68: require explicit `--legacy`; their receipts cannot establish current-standard
69: acceptance. Do not silently migrate, overwrite, or relabel old cases. The
70: archived case-2 authoring script no longer manufactures passing reviews.
71: The [format example](../../tests/fixtures/closed-addition/nl0.json) is a small schema
72: example with an unperformed audit, not a new benchmark or certification.
73: 
74: ## Verdicts and invalidation
75: 
76: - `STRUCTURE-PASSED`: schema, graph, explicit references, frozen specification,
77:   and definition prerequisites passed the mechanical checks.
78: - `AUDIT-RECEIPT-VALID`: a complete, matching audit record was checked. This is
79:   an evidence/coverage verdict, not the program proving the mathematics.
80: - `DRAFT-AUDIT-PASSED`: the named auditor actually completed Audit A for every
81:   source, definition, inference, and target obligation. Report whether the
82:   auditor shared context with the author; never relabel self-audit as an
83:   independent review or Lean verification.
84: - `DRAFT-AUDIT-CONDITIONAL`: complete review relative to explicit external
85:   statements whose primary sources remain unverified. Preserve the source
86:   warnings and follow the [conditional-source policy](conditional-sources.md).
87: - `GAP`, `SOURCE-MISMATCH`, `TARGET-MISMATCH`, `ASSUMPTION-MISMATCH`, `INVALID`,
88:   or `UNVERIFIED`: identify the exact failing obligation and affected closure.
89: 
90: Bind audit records to the canonical graph/spec hashes and evidence file hashes.
91: Changed claims, inputs, arguments, definitions, assumptions, or sources revoke
92: the affected verdicts. Reuse is limited to previously qualified unchanged items
93: whose current content, dependencies, review scope and evidence bindings still
94: verify. Changed or newly required items need actual review; missing or stale
95: evidence cannot grant acceptance. Preserve the earlier findings and failed
96: reports. Never add the missing conclusion as an H, source theorem, definition
97: property, structure field, or typeclass merely to close the graph.
98: 
99: ## Deliver
100: 
101: Deliver the frozen specification, canonical graph, readable view, bipartite
102: diagram, primary-source/signature evidence, per-object Audit A, mechanical
103: results, and the first remaining gap. Describe functional smoke tests and

6: module
7: 
8: public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.DirectSum.Finsupp
9: public import Mathlib.RingTheory.IsTensorProduct
10: public import Mathlib.RingTheory.Localization.Away.Basic
11: public import Mathlib.RingTheory.Localization.Module
12: 
13: /-!
14: # Localized Module
15: 
16: Given a commutative semiring `R`, a multiplicative subset `S ⊆ R` and an `R`-module `M`, we can
17: localize `M` by `S`. This gives us a `Localization S`-module.
18: 
19: ## Main definition
20: 
21: * `isLocalizedModule_iff_isBaseChange` : A localization of modules corresponds to a base change.
22: -/
23: 
24: @[expose] public section
25: 
26: variable {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R] (S : Submonoid R)
27:   (A : Type*) [CommSemiring A] [Algebra R A] [IsLocalization S A]
28:   {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M]
29:   {M' : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M'] [Module R M'] [Module A M'] [IsScalarTower R A M']
30:   (f : M →ₗ[R] M')
31: 
32: /-- The forward direction of `isLocalizedModule_iff_isBaseChange`. It is also used to prove the
33: other direction. -/
34: theorem IsLocalizedModule.isBaseChange [IsLocalizedModule S f] : IsBaseChange A f :=
35:   .of_lift_unique _ fun Q _ _ _ _ g ↦ by
36:     obtain ⟨ℓ, rfl, h₂⟩ := IsLocalizedModule.is_universal S f g fun s ↦ by
37:       rw [← (Algebra.lsmul R (A := A) R Q).commutes]; exact (IsLocalization.map_units A s).map _
38:     refine ⟨ℓ.extendScalarsOfIsLocalization S A, by simp, fun g'' h ↦ ?_⟩
39:     cases h₂ (LinearMap.restrictScalars R g'') h; rfl
40: 
41: variable (M) in
42: lemma LocalizedModule.isBaseChange :
43:     IsBaseChange (Localization S) (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap S M) :=
44:   IsLocalizedModule.isBaseChange S (Localization S) (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap S M)
45: 
46: /-- The map `(f : M →ₗ[R] M')` is a localization of modules iff the map
47: `(Localization S) × M → N, (s, m) ↦ s • f m` is the tensor product (insomuch as it is the universal
48: bilinear map).
49: In particular, there is an isomorphism between `LocalizedModule S M` and `(Localization S) ⊗[R] M`
50: given by `m/s ↦ (1/s) ⊗ₜ m`.
51: -/
52: theorem isLocalizedModule_iff_isBaseChange : IsLocalizedModule S f ↔ IsBaseChange A f := by
53:   refine ⟨fun _ ↦ IsLocalizedModule.isBaseChange S A f, fun h ↦ ?_⟩
54:   letI : Module A (LocalizedModule S M) := LocalizedModule.moduleOfIsLocalization ..
55:   have : IsBaseChange A (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap S M) := IsLocalizedModule.isBaseChange S A _
56:   let e := (this.equiv.symm.trans h.equiv).restrictScalars R
57:   convert! IsLocalizedModule.of_linearEquiv S (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap S M) e
58:   ext
59:   rw [LinearMap.coe_comp, LinearEquiv.coe_coe, Function.comp_apply,
60:     LinearEquiv.restrictScalars_apply, LinearEquiv.trans_apply, IsBaseChange.equiv_symm_apply,
61:     IsBaseChange.equiv_tmul, one_smul]
62: 
63: open TensorProduct
64: 
65: variable (M) in
66: /-- The localization of an `R`-module `M` at a submonoid `S` is isomorphic to `S⁻¹R ⊗[R] M` as
67: an `S⁻¹R`-module. -/
68: noncomputable def LocalizedModule.equivTensorProduct :
69:     LocalizedModule S M ≃ₗ[Localization S] Localization S ⊗[R] M :=
70:   (LocalizedModule.isBaseChange S M).equiv.symm
71: 
72: @[simp]
73: lemma LocalizedModule.equivTensorProduct_symm_apply_tmul (x : M) (r : R) (s : S) :
74:     (equivTensorProduct S M).symm (Localization.mk r s ⊗ₜ[R] x) = r • mk x s := by
75:   simp [equivTensorProduct, IsBaseChange.equiv_tmul, mk_smul_mk, smul'_mk]
76: 
77: @[simp]
78: lemma LocalizedModule.equivTensorProduct_symm_apply_tmul_one (x : M) :
79:     (equivTensorProduct S M).symm (1 ⊗ₜ[R] x) = mk x 1 := by
80:   simp [← Localization.mk_one]
81: 
82: @[simp]
83: lemma LocalizedModule.equivTensorProduct_apply_mk (x : M) (s : S) :
84:     equivTensorProduct S M (mk x s) = Localization.mk 1 s ⊗ₜ[R] x := by
85:   apply (equivTensorProduct S M).symm.injective
86:   simp
87: 
88: attribute [local instance] Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra in
89: instance {T : Type*} [CommSemiring T] [Algebra R T] :
90:     IsLocalizedModule S (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R T (A ⊗[R] T) : T →ₗ[R] A ⊗[R] T) := by
91:   rw [isLocalizedModule_iff_isBaseChange (S := S) (A := A)]
92:   exact TensorProduct.isBaseChange _ _ _
93: 
94: namespace IsLocalization
95: 
96: open TensorProduct Algebra.TensorProduct
97: 
98: instance tensorProduct_isLocalizedModule : IsLocalizedModule S (TensorProduct.mk R A M 1) :=
99:   (isLocalizedModule_iff_isBaseChange _ A _).mpr (TensorProduct.isBaseChange _ _ _)
100: 
101: variable (M₁ M₂ B C) [AddCommMonoid M₁] [AddCommMonoid M₂] [Module R M₁] [Module R M₂]
102:   [Module A M₁] [Module A M₂] [IsScalarTower R A M₁] [IsScalarTower R A M₂]
103:   [Semiring B] [Algebra R B] [Algebra A B] [IsScalarTower R A B]
104:   [Semiring C] [Algebra R C] [Algebra A C] [IsScalarTower R A C]
105: include S
106: 
107: theorem tensorProduct_compatibleSMul : CompatibleSMul R A M₁ M₂ where
108:   smul_tmul a _ _ := by
109:     obtain ⟨r, s, rfl⟩ := exists_mk'_eq S a
110:     rw [← (map_units A s).smul_left_cancel]
111:     simp_rw [algebraMap_smul, smul_tmul', ← smul_assoc, smul_tmul, ← smul_assoc, smul_mk'_self,
112:       algebraMap_smul, smul_tmul]
113: 
114: instance [Module (Localization S) M₁] [Module (Localization S) M₂]
115:     [IsScalarTower R (Localization S) M₁] [IsScalarTower R (Localization S) M₂] :
116:     CompatibleSMul R (Localization S) M₁ M₂ :=
117:   tensorProduct_compatibleSMul S ..
118: 
119: instance (N N') [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R N] [AddCommMonoid N'] [Module R N'] (g : N →ₗ[R] N')
120:     [IsLocalizedModule S f] [IsLocalizedModule S g] :
121:     IsLocalizedModule S (TensorProduct.map f g) := by
122:   let eM := IsLocalizedModule.linearEquiv S f (TensorProduct.mk R (Localization S) M 1)
123:   let eN := IsLocalizedModule.linearEquiv S g (TensorProduct.mk R (Localization S) N 1)
124:   convert!
125:     IsLocalizedModule.of_linearEquiv S (TensorProduct.mk R (Localization S) (M ⊗[R] N) 1) <|
126:       (AlgebraTensorModule.distribBaseChange R (Localization S) ..).restrictScalars R ≪≫ₗ
127:         (congr eM eN ≪≫ₗ TensorProduct.equivOfCompatibleSMul ..).symm
128:   ext; congrm (?_ ⊗ₜ ?_) <;> simp [LinearEquiv.eq_symm_apply, eM, eN]
129: 
130: /-- If `A` is a localization of `R`, tensoring two `A`-modules over `A` is the same as
131: tensoring them over `R`. -/
132: noncomputable def moduleTensorEquiv : M₁ ⊗[A] M₂ ≃ₗ[A] M₁ ⊗[R] M₂ :=
133:   have := tensorProduct_compatibleSMul S A M₁ M₂
134:   equivOfCompatibleSMul R A A M₁ M₂
135: 
136: /-- If `A` is a localization of `R`, tensoring an `A`-module with `A` over `R` does nothing. -/
137: noncomputable def moduleLid : A ⊗[R] M₁ ≃ₗ[A] M₁ :=
138:   have := tensorProduct_compatibleSMul S A A M₁
139:   (equivOfCompatibleSMul R A A A M₁).symm ≪≫ₗ TensorProduct.lid _ _
140: 
141: /-- If `A` is a localization of `R`, tensoring two `A`-algebras over `A` is the same as
142: tensoring them over `R`. -/
143: noncomputable def algebraTensorEquiv : B ⊗[A] C ≃ₐ[A] B ⊗[R] C :=
144:   have := tensorProduct_compatibleSMul S A B C
145:   Algebra.TensorProduct.equivOfCompatibleSMul R A A B C
146: 
147: /-- If `A` is a localization of `R`, tensoring an `A`-algebra with `A` over `R` does nothing. -/
148: noncomputable def algebraLid : A ⊗[R] B ≃ₐ[A] B :=
149:   have := tensorProduct_compatibleSMul S A A B
150:   Algebra.TensorProduct.lidOfCompatibleSMul R A B
151: 
152: set_option linter.docPrime false in
153: theorem bijective_linearMap_mul' : Function.Bijective (LinearMap.mul' R A) :=
154:   have := tensorProduct_compatibleSMul S A A A
155:   (Algebra.TensorProduct.lmulEquiv R A).bijective
156: 
157: end IsLocalization
158: 
159: variable (T B : Type*) [CommSemiring T] [CommSemiring B]
160:   [Algebra R T] [Algebra T B] [Algebra R B] [Algebra A B] [IsScalarTower R T B]
161:   [IsScalarTower R A B]
162: 
163: variable {T B} in
164: lemma Algebra.isLocalization_iff_isPushout :
165:     IsLocalization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid T S) B ↔ IsPushout R T A B := by
166:   rw [Algebra.IsPushout.comm, Algebra.isPushout_iff, ← isLocalizedModule_iff_isLocalization]
167:   rw [← isLocalizedModule_iff_isBaseChange (S := S)]
168: 
169: lemma Algebra.isPushout_of_isLocalization [IsLocalization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid T S) B] :
170:     Algebra.IsPushout R T A B :=

13: /-!
14: # Bases and dimensionality of tensor products of modules
15: 
16: This file defines various bases on the tensor product of modules,
17: and shows that the tensor product of free modules is again free.
18: -/
19:

37: /-- If `b : ι → M` and `c : κ → N` are bases then so is `fun i ↦ b i.1 ⊗ₜ c i.2 : ι × κ → M ⊗ N`. -/
38: def tensorProduct (b : Basis ι S M) (c : Basis κ R N) :
39:     Basis (ι × κ) S (M ⊗[R] N) :=
40:   Finsupp.basisSingleOne.map
41:     ((TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.congr b.repr c.repr).trans <|
42:         (finsuppTensorFinsupp R S _ _ _ _).trans <|
43:           Finsupp.lcongr (Equiv.refl _) (TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.rid R S S)).symm
44: 
45: @[simp]
46: theorem tensorProduct_apply (b : Basis ι S M) (c : Basis κ R N) (i : ι) (j : κ) :
47:     tensorProduct b c (i, j) = b i ⊗ₜ c j := by
48:   simp [tensorProduct]
49: 
50: theorem tensorProduct_apply' (b : Basis ι S M) (c : Basis κ R N) (i : ι × κ) :
51:     tensorProduct b c i = b i.1 ⊗ₜ c i.2 := by
52:   simp [tensorProduct]
53: 
54: @[simp]
55: theorem tensorProduct_repr_tmul_apply (b : Basis ι S M) (c : Basis κ R N) (m : M) (n : N)
56:     (i : ι) (j : κ) :
57:     (tensorProduct b c).repr (m ⊗ₜ n) (i, j) = c.repr n j • b.repr m i := by
58:   simp [tensorProduct]
59: 
60: variable (S : Type*) [Semiring S] [Algebra R S]
61: 
62: /-- The lift of an `R`-basis of `M` to an `S`-basis of the base change `S ⊗[R] M`. -/
63: noncomputable
64: def baseChange (b : Basis ι R M) : Basis ι S (S ⊗[R] M) :=
65:   (tensorProduct (.singleton Unit S) b).reindex (Equiv.punitProd ι)
66: 
67: @[simp]
68: lemma baseChange_repr_tmul (b : Basis ι R M) (x y i) :
69:     (b.baseChange S).repr (x ⊗ₜ y) i = b.repr y i • x := by
70:   simp [baseChange, tensorProduct]
71: 
72: @[simp]
73: lemma baseChange_apply (b : Basis ι R M) (i) :
74:     b.baseChange S i = 1 ⊗ₜ b i := by
75:   simp [baseChange, tensorProduct]
76: 
77: end Module.Basis
